newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to be cautious on foreign currency bond.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to be cautious on foreign currency bond.

text.p: Ukraine's first issue of foreign-currency bonds is likely to be a "cautious" issue of short-term paper to win the international financial community's confidence, a top adviser to President Leonid Kuchma said.
Valery Lytvytsky told Reuters late on Wednesday the first issue would be tantamount to an "examination" for Ukraine.

"Under no circumstances do we want our debut to be a failure and for that reason the first bond issue will be limited and carefully prepared," he said. He said subsequent issues could be medium and long-term.
Lytvytsky said the bond issue, planned for 1997, did not figure in the 1997 budget.
He said a projected fall in 1997 inflation to 24.9 percent from this year's forecast 48 percent would enable Ukraine to "conduct transactions on the world financial market".

Central Bank Chairman Viktor Yushchenko has said that a bond issue next year is a vital part of the government's strategy to maintain its budget deficit at 4.0 percent -- 2.4 percent using Western methods.
He also said several Western institutions had already made enquiries about acting as an agent to offer Ukrainian bonds on international markets.
